properties.decision: What the reader sees, for a position derived from a principle. Built (the skill's recipe): the step takes the principle in `assumed`, so the position reads "conditional: holds under this principle", a position several principles support names each, but an objection against the principle is read on the principle only (the positions already say they hold only if it does), and a what-if on the principle says nothing about the positions. Options: (a) assumed, as built — matches what the trolley trial's designer did and its observer expected; (b) taken as given — positions read plain "holds" (shown), an objection against a principle contests every position on it, and a what-if on it works. Recommended: (a). It is wrong if Anthony wants an objection to a principle to reach every position resting on it now, rather than after the later phase 6 PR on contested foundations.

properties.rationale:
The skill has to pick one recipe so its readings agree with the tools. (a) is the honest one for "positions on principles" (each is a result inside an argument from a chosen principle); (b) reads better under objections and what-ifs today. Later phase 6 PRs (a contested foundation reads contested; a what-if on a premise reaches what rests on it) narrow the gap either way.
